summary: Peggy's Point light on the east side of St. Margaret's Bay; the concrete tower of 1915 stands beside the old wooden light, kept as the keeper's house.

structures.type: wooden dwelling with lantern on its roof
structures.status: replaced 1915; kept as keeper's residence without its lantern room
structures.note: Contract for the lighthouse awarded 20 June 1867; first keeper listed from 1868 (LighthouseFriends). Completion date not stated in the sources read.

access.note: LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. The register describes the rock as having no visible paths to the tower.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (Government of Canada per the record); a viewing platform opened near the light in 2021

events.note: Board of Works awards a $1,690 contract to Murphy and Lawlor on 20 June 1867 to build the lighthouse
First keeper Edward Horne listed from 1868 (LighthouseFriends); no first-light date is stated in the sources read
Heavy southeast gale on 15 April 1881: a heavy sea broke over the point, damaging the lighthouse and foundation and sweeping away the oil house; repairs cost $545
Eight-sided iron lantern room, formerly used at West Ironbound Island, replaced the old lantern room
Fifth-order lens installed on 29 March 1897 in place of lamps and reflectors
Explosion in the lantern room, less than three months after the lens was installed, damaged the lens; old apparatus put back
Concrete octagonal tower built by the Standard Construction Company of Halifax under a $2,456 contract; placed in operation 1 August 1915
Fourth-order lens and an eight-foot lantern, $1,945.92
Hurricane Edna caused extensive damage to the original lighthouse
Time switch installed to control the beacon; light made unwatched; caretaker hired April 1958
Swissair Flight 111 crashed just offshore (LighthouseFriends note; memorial on the Lighthouse Route about a kilometre away)
New accessible viewing platform opened near the lighthouse in October 2021

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1868 (Rowlett) is the first keeper's listing in LighthouseFriends; the sources read give no first-light date. The concrete tower was built in 1915 (LighthouseFriends; Coast Guard list shows the present light).
The record's F G (OpenStreetMap) is not the current light. The Coast Guard list gives Fl R 5s for H3660 and its position matches the record's coordinates.

notes_for_editor: (1) Tower height: LighthouseFriends says about 30 ft (9 m); the Coast Guard list gives 13.2 m. The story gives both; the record uses 13.2. (2) Heritage designation: the record's 2002 comes from Wikidata. The register page as read did not show a recognition date, so the story gives none. Check the register before adding a date. (3) First light: no source read gives a first-light date. LighthouseFriends lists Edward Horne as first keeper from 1868 and reports the Board of Works contract of 20 June 1867; the story uses those and does not say when the light first shone. The 1874, 1881 and 1897 facts come from LighthouseFriends quoting Department reports that are not in the local corpus (the corpus starts in 1900); footnoted to LighthouseFriends only. (4) Names: LighthouseFriends spells Sidney; the Department's lists print Sidney/Sydney H. Garrison. The 1905 keeper list line 'Garrison, S. H / Peggy Point / Dec. 22, 1902' was matched by position in the OCR and checked on the page image (scan p.343, printed p.262): the row reads 'Garrison, S. H., Peggy Point' with appointment 22 December 1902. (5) Nellie G. Garrison: LighthouseFriends' list is the only source for her; no relation to the Garrisons is stated. (6) York Manuel's caretaker dates (1958 to 1966) come only from LighthouseFriends. He is named in his public role only. (7) Hurricane Edna damage and the 1954 demolition are LighthouseFriends only. (8) The Swissair 111 reference is LighthouseFriends' note; the story claims no lighthouse role in the crash. (9) A Chronicling America search for 'Peggy's Cove' with 'lighthouse' returned nothing relevant. (10) The 1921 Halifax agency report lists 'Peggy point' among stations repaired that year; not used.
